purpose: Prevent genus-level master taxa from absorbing species- or plant-part-specific nutrition records.
principles: Do not broaden a species-specific nutrient record to a genus-level master taxon.
Do not merge leaf, flower, fruit, pad, seed or sprout records.
Do not merge raw and cooked/dried records.
Keep original source taxon and food description visible.

cases.recommended_resolution: split only if product scope requires species-level nutrition; candidate species records such as Mentha spicata remain comparative until split policy is approved.
separate white/red clover if nutrition data are to be displayed; forage dry-matter records remain separate.
fresh petals must be separated from rose hips and from species-specific Rosa hybrida studies.
resolve exact Cucurbita species before promoting leaf nutrient records.
separate fruit from pads and resolve species before promoting numeric records.
retain color-specific records separately; do not average colors.

release_rule: No master-taxonomy change is made by inference. Any split must be explicitly justified by the food identity used by the site and supported by source records.

checks: exact master taxon versus source taxon
whether master split is actually necessary
next_validation_batch.promotion_rule: Only after all checks pass may a candidate enter plant_nutrition_v56.json.

validation_result.interpretation: These five remain genuine enrichment targets in the verified nutrition layer. Candidate source records documented elsewhere are not yet sufficient for promotion.
validation_result.next: Continue original-record reconciliation and do not duplicate existing records.
